provenance.method: two-proportion pooled z-test (NIST/SEMATECH §7.3.3, Case 1) + Newcombe (1998) method-10 risk-difference CI

assumptions_checked: n*phat >= 5 and n*(1-phat) >= 5 per sample cleared (matrix §4a EXIT-06)
value.effect_size_ci_method: Newcombe (1998) method 10, built from per-sample Wilson score intervals

plain_language.comparison_summary: Compared the proportion for baseline (90/1379 = 6.5%) against settled_weeks (19/753 = 2.5%) using a two-proportion z-test.
plain_language.effect_size_in_words: Risk difference = +4.0% (baseline minus settled_weeks), 95% CI [+2.2%, +5.7%] (Newcombe's method).
plain_language.p_value_meaning: p = 0.0001, below the alpha=0.05 threshold: if there were truly no difference, a result at least this far from 'no difference' would turn up by chance alone only about 0.006% of the time. That makes the difference statistically detectable here -- it does not mean the null hypothesis is false with that probability, and it says nothing yet about whether the difference is big enough to matter.
plain_language.practical_significance_prompt: Statistically detectable ≠ big enough to matter -- compare the effect size above against the goal.
